title: How to Save Tax in India for Salaried Employees (FY 2025-26): The Ultimate Guide
excerpt: Maximize your take-home pay with our definitive guide on tax saving for salaried employees in India for FY 2025-26. Learn about Section 80C, 80D, HRA, and the New vs Old Tax Regime.
content:
Are you looking for the best ways to save tax in India for salaried employees in FY 2025-26? With the recent changes in the Union Budget, navigating the Indian income tax system can feel like a maze. However, with the right planning, you can significantly reduce your tax liability and maximize your take-home pay.

In this comprehensive guide, we will break down the most effective tax-saving strategies, compare the Old vs New Tax Regime for 2025-26, and show you how to use a salary calculator to plan your finances perfectly.

1. Understanding the Tax Regimes: Old vs. New (FY 2025-26)

The first step in your tax-saving journey is choosing the right regime. For the financial year 2025-26, the New Tax Regime remains the default option, but the Old Regime is still available for those with significant investments.

New Tax Regime Highlights:

  • Higher Standard Deduction: Increased to ₹75,000.
  • Revised Tax Slabs: Lower tax rates for middle-income earners.
  • Tax Rebate: No tax on income up to ₹7 lakh (effectively ₹7.75 lakh with standard deduction).

Old Tax Regime Highlights:

  • Deductions Galore: Allows you to claim Section 80C, 80D, HRA, and LTA.
  • Best for High Savers: If your total deductions exceed ₹3.75 lakh, the Old Regime might still be better.
Pro Tip: Before deciding, use the Salary Calculator at salarycalc.in to compare both regimes based on your specific salary structure. It’s the fastest way to see which one saves you more money!

2. Top Section 80C Investment Options (Limit: ₹1.5 Lakh)

Section 80C is the most popular tax-saving tool for salaried individuals. You can claim a deduction of up to ₹1.5 lakh by investing in:

3. Maximizing HRA and Home Loan Benefits

If you are living in a rented house, House Rent Allowance (HRA) is a powerful tool to reduce your taxable income under the Old Regime.

Additionally, if you have a home loan, you can claim:

  • Section 24(b): Up to ₹2 lakh on interest paid.
  • Section 80C: Principal repayment (within the ₹1.5 lakh limit).

4. Health Insurance and Section 80D

Don't overlook your health! Under Section 80D, you can claim deductions for health insurance premiums:

  • Self, Spouse, and Children: Up to ₹25,000 (₹50,000 if senior citizens).
  • Parents: Additional ₹25,000 (₹50,000 if they are senior citizens).

This means a total deduction of up to ₹75,000 to ₹1,00,000 is possible just by securing your family's health.

5. The Power of NPS (National Pension System)

The NPS offers an additional deduction of ₹50,000 under Section 80CCD(1B), over and above the ₹1.5 lakh limit of Section 80C. This is a great way to build a retirement corpus while saving extra tax.

6. How to Calculate Your Take-Home Salary?

Knowing your "Gross Salary" is one thing, but knowing your "Net Take-Home" is what matters for your monthly budget. Tax deductions, PF contributions, and professional tax can be confusing to calculate manually.

To get an accurate breakdown of your monthly in-hand salary, visit salarycalc.in. This tool is specifically designed for Indian employees to handle the latest FY 2025-26 tax rules, including the new slabs and standard deductions.

Conclusion: Start Planning Early!

Tax saving is not a year-end activity; it’s a year-long strategy. By choosing the right regime and investing in the right instruments, you can save lakhs in taxes.

Summary Checklist for FY 2025-26:

  1. Compare regimes on salarycalc.in.
  2. Maximize your 80C limit (₹1.5L).
  3. Invest in NPS for an extra ₹50k deduction.
  4. Secure your family with Health Insurance (80D).
  5. Keep your rent receipts ready for HRA claims.

Disclaimer: Tax laws are subject to change. Always consult with a certified tax professional before making major financial decisions.
